prompt.context: Rock Energy is an Oil & Gas company evaluating the purchase of one of three oil fields in Latin America. After Rock Energy has decided which oil field to purchase, it will outsource all drilling-related activities.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate the three oil fields, and which oil field should Rock Energy purchase?

clarifying_info.q: How long does the drilling rights agreement last?
clarifying_info.a: The rights give Rock Energy the right to drill during year 1 and produce oil for 20 years. No oil is produced until the beginning of year 2.

clarifying_info.q: How many rigs can be deployed?
clarifying_info.a: The drilling operator can deploy a maximum of 10 rigs in each of the regions concurrently.

clarifying_info.q: What is included in the rig day cost?
clarifying_info.a: The cost per rig day includes crew, consumables, and services.
Any amount of oil extracted will be sold at the spot market price at the moment.

clarifying_info.q: Are there maintenance costs on the wells?
clarifying_info.a: For simplicity, assume the oil wells will produce the same amount of oil for the next 20 years with no maintenance costs.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost to secure the rights?
clarifying_info.a: The rights to extract oil cost $40M in each region.

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of oil?

exhibits.title: Oil Field Profiles, 2010
exhibits.shows: A table comparing three regions across drilling rate (meters/day), average depth of wells (meters), maximum number of rigs operating concurrently, average well production (barrels per day), and cost per rig day.

data.note: Wells are continuously dug during year 1 (assume 360 days). Oil is extracted beginning of year 2. Once a well is completed the rig moves on to dig another.

framework: Define evaluation criteria: profitability (revenue vs. cost), strategic fit, and risk
Calculate time to complete one well per region (Depth / Penetration Rate)
Calculate cost per well (Days to complete well x Cost per rig day)
Calculate number of wells drillable in year 1 (360 days / time per well x number of rigs)
Calculate yearly revenue per well (Price per barrel x barrels per day x 360 days)
Calculate total revenue and total cost per region
Compute profit per region (Total Revenue - Total Cost including rights)
Assess qualitative factors and risks before making a recommendation

questions.prompt: Calculate the time to complete one well in each region (in days).
questions.guidance: Divide the average depth by the drilling rate (penetration rate). Region 1: 1200/20=60 days. Region 2: 2700/30=90 days. Region 3: 3600/20=180 days.

math.setup: Time to complete a well (days) = Average depth (meters) / Drilling rate (meters/day)
math.answer: Region 1 = 60 days, Region 2 = 90 days, Region 3 = 180 days

questions.prompt: Calculate the cost per well in each region.
questions.guidance: Multiply days to complete the well by the cost per rig day. Region 1: 60x$5,000=$300K. Region 2: 90x$10,000=$900K. Region 3: 180x$20,000=$3.6M.

math.setup: Cost per well = Days to complete well x Cost per rig day

questions.prompt: Calculate how many wells can be drilled in year 1 per region (all 10 rigs working 360 days).
questions.guidance: Number of wells = (360 / days per well) x number of rigs. Region 1: (360/60)x10=60. Region 2: (360/90)x10=40. Region 3: (360/180)x10=20.

math.setup: Number of wells per year = (360 days / Time to complete one well) x Number of rigs
math.answer: Region 1 = 60 wells, Region 2 = 40 wells, Region 3 = 20 wells

questions.prompt: Calculate yearly revenue per well and profit per well in each region (using oil price of $50/bbl).
questions.guidance: Yearly revenue per well = Price x barrels/day x 360. Profit per well = Revenue per well - Cost per well. Region 1: Revenue $1.8M, Cost $300K, Profit $1.5M (500% margin). Region 2: Revenue $3.6M, Cost $900K, Profit $2.7M (300% margin). Region 3: Revenue $5.4M, Cost $3.6M, Profit $1.8M (50% margin).

math.setup: Yearly Revenue per well = $50/bbl x Production (bpd) x 360 days; Profit per well = Revenue per well - Cost per well
math.answer: Region 1: $1.5M profit/well (500% margin); Region 2: $2.7M profit/well (300% margin); Region 3: $1.8M profit/well (50% margin)

questions.prompt: Calculate total revenue, total cost, and total profit for the first year of production across all wells in each region (include the $40M rights cost).
questions.guidance: Total Revenue = Revenue per well x number of wells. Total Cost = (Cost per well x number of wells) + $40M rights. Profit = Total Revenue - Total Cost. Region 2 is the most profitable at $68M.

math.setup: Total Revenue = Yearly revenue per well x Number of wells; Total Cost = (Cost per well x Number of wells) + $40M rights; Profit = Total Revenue - Total Cost

brainstorming.prompt: What other qualitative factors or risks could affect the investment decision across the three regions?

categories.name: Political & Regulatory Risk
ideas: Government policy on foreign oil extraction

categories.name: Operational Risk
ideas: Availability and reliability of the outsourced drilling operator

categories.name: Market Risk
ideas: Volatility of oil prices (price used is $50/bbl spot)
Currency risk if revenues/costs are in different currencies
Demand shifts affecting spot price over 20-year production horizon

categories.name: Geological & Technical Risk
ideas: Oil quality differences between regions (light vs. heavy crude, sulfur content)
Probability distribution of actual barrels extracted vs. expected (expected value analysis)
Unexpected depth or penetration rate variations

categories.name: Strategic Fit
ideas: Alignment with Rock Energys portfolio strategy
Option value of adjacent acreage in each region

recommendation: Rock Energy should purchase the rights to Region 2, which generates the highest first-year profit of $68M versus $50M for Region 1 and a loss of $4M for Region 3

Although Region 1 has a superior profit margin per well (500% vs. 300%), Region 2 drills 40 wells in year 1 compared to 60 for Region 1 but at much higher revenue per well, yielding greater total profit; Region 3 is loss-making at current oil prices
risks: Oil price volatility could erode margins; a significant price drop below ~$30/bbl would threaten Region 2 profitability
Political instability or regulatory changes in the Latin American region could impair operations
Actual geological conditions may differ from profiles, affecting penetration rates and production volumes
next_steps: Conduct an expected value analysis assigning probabilities to different production outcomes per region
Assess political and regulatory environment in each country before finalizing the investment
Negotiate insurance and labor contracts for the outsourced drilling operator
Model 20-year NPV incorporating oil price scenarios and discount rate
